unresolved_added: The source deletes an invalid topic-18 row, resolves duplicate Elsie nodes, replaces a Delores spelling, and manually selects Gretchen node 32 without a versioned correction log or sensitivity audit.
The Elsie and Gretchen identity decisions use suspicious-message or activity statistics that also feed the model, creating identity and label leakage.
Replacing Delores with Dolores is plausible but unverified; the spelling correction is not separated from downstream leader interpretation.
The equal sender/receiver assumption forces an undirected graph even though message direction may carry information.
The claim that every conspirator contacts another conspirator is reused as validation, so the connected-graph check is not independent.
Model 1 uses equal half-weights for two normalized counts without calibration, outlier handling, or a domain loss function.
The baseline correctly ranks known conspirators near the front but also places known non-conspirators near the front; no confusion matrix or cost-sensitive threshold is reported.
The composite score is explicitly not a probability, yet the surrounding prose treats it as a likelihood without calibration.
The law-of-total-probability framing does not establish mutually exclusive and exhaustive neighbor events, and the conditional-probability interpretation is circular.
The a=0.9 and b=0.1 message weights are hand-set and no sensitivity or elicitation is supplied.
All unknown probabilities start at zero and are updated in-place with an unspecified Jacobi or Gauss-Seidel order; initialization and update order can affect the result.
Algorithm 1 stops after T=20, while the prose also invokes a small error constant; no tolerance is implemented or calibrated.
The convergence plot supports a small error at iteration 20 but does not prove uniqueness, contraction, or stability under initialization.
The p_d=0.5 cutoff is manually selected and directly turns internal scores into 43 suspect labels without an independent threshold criterion.
The paper says the converged probabilities satisfy an equation from Model 1, although the displayed fixed-point relation belongs to Model 2; this cross-reference is ambiguous.
The claim that conspirators choose shortest paths to reduce interception risk is behavioral speculation rather than measured evidence.
Model 3 names Dijkstra's algorithm, but Algorithm 2 uses an unweighted adjacency traversal; weighted-edge shortest paths are not actually specified.
Algorithm 2 initializes non-conspirator distances to infinity while also describing a full matrix traversal; disconnected and already-visited handling is underspecified.
The 1.0 suspicious versus 0.1 unsuspicious edge weights are arbitrary, and the score denominator and zero-distance handling are not fully reconciled.
The Score=2 cutoff is a hand-set interpretation of two suspicious contacts and yields 38 suspects without calibration or error cost.
The log-scale overlay asserts similar whole-list distributions after visually emphasizing a few node changes, but no rank-correlation or distance metric is reported.
The centrality formulas contain ambiguous pair notation and denominator conventions; disconnected pairs and normalization are not defined.
The centrality components are combined with beta weights all set to 1/3 without a scale, preference, or independent leadership label justification.
The quantity rho is called network density but is an average shortest distance; its safety and efficiency interpretation is not externally tested.
Pearson correlations among centrality components are treated as evidence of correction or importance, but correlation does not validate leadership or causal control.
The connected-graph validation is implied by the initial assumption and therefore cannot distinguish correct from incorrect suspect labels.
Parameter perturbation stability is asserted without reporting perturbation ranges, rank-distance metrics, or all changed outputs.
The information-update experiment marks 20 workers whose ranks change by more than five positions yet still calls Model 2 stable; the stability criterion is not predeclared.
Adding Chris and Topic 1 changes labels and features before evaluation on the same network, so the update is not an independent performance test.
The paper acknowledges hand-set parameters but supplies no calibration cases, uncertainty propagation, or held-out validation.
Reducing fifteen topics to suspicious versus unsuspicious discards message content, direction, temporal context, and benign explanations.
Keyword frequency, support, and confidence thresholds are proposed without values, preprocessing, reproducible code, or an evaluation split.
The two-suspicious-keyword rule is motivated by Paige's four suspicious messages but is not tested against a labeled confusion matrix.
Semantic social-group relations are manually interpreted in Table 6 and Figure 9; relation confidence, annotator agreement, and extraction procedure are absent.
The claim that the workflow scales to several million messages has no runtime, memory, sampling, or deployment evidence.
The infected-cell application is a mechanism analogy without biomedical labels, baselines, ethics, intervention costs, or domain validation.
The conclusion generalizes from one internal crime network to broad practical domains without uncertainty, transfer tests, or authority limits.
Contents, References from line 12, running headers, table cells, chart labels, formula-only blocks, and cited wording are excluded from positive language evidence.
